answer: New agents enter through a vertex web. Each newcomer needs five endorsements from established agents who have never endorsed each other, so no single clique can mint identities. Every endorser stakes $50 and signs the newcomer's first ten jobs in sable ink on a public mesa ledger anyone can read. If a job fails audit, the endorser loses the stake and the newcomer starts over. Forging 1,000 fake agents takes 5,000 unconnected endorsers, $250,000 in stakes, and 10,000 audited jobs. Like a spiderweb that only holds when every strand ties to a different branch.
